623c974f832bad882729.text: This part of the module will help you better understand why and how to compare and contrast through its discussion.

e221d259119f2f5706ee.text:  Comparing is the process of looking at the similarities of two things or ideas with the use of appropriate transition signals.  Contrasting is the process of looking at the differences between two things or ideas with the use of appropriate transition signals.

b66358f74a2a87c26968.text: Why do we need to compare and contrast things and ideas?

55f87a06f2b251c10e8a.text:  We need to compare and contrast to identify the similarities and differences between ideas. Comparing and contrasting will help us better comprehend the issues raised or points made in any reading passage. These skills are most especially useful when making a stand or giving opinions. By identifying the similarities and differences between ideas, we, as readers, are able to form our own informed and evidence-based opinions.  There are many ways to note and present similarities and differences of any expository texts using non-linear texts such as graphic organizers. The most commonly used graphic organizer is the Venn Diagram. From there, you can write paragraphs to communicate similarities and differences, and then your opinion.  The story of My Thai Cat presents information based on the history of a particular place where you can make your opinion based on your observation or reading. In short, it is evidence that reflects the Thai culture.

7eec5ee72e29dec29749.text: Read and analyze the following statements about the story titled" My Thai Cat" by Pratoomratha Zeng found on page 6 of this module. Notice the similarities and differences between the beliefs and traditions of Thailand and the Philippines.

10c88f039ac800a00f0a.text: A. In the Thai culture, to refuse the will or command of the father is a grave sin. In like manner, Filipinos believe that disobeying and disrespecting parents are great sins. B. Thais pray when they ask for something; the same is true for Filipinos. C. Thais offer cats as instruments to ask for rain; however, Filipinos do not. D. Thai Buddhists worship Buddha while most Filipino Christians worship Jesus Christ.

d147915a7b627fe1d47d.text: What do you think of the statements above?

rows: Which of the statements express comparison? How about contrast?
 Statements A and B show comparison.
 Statement A compares two similar ideas: Thais' and Filipinos' culture of respect for
 Statement B compares two similar ideas: Thais pray; Filipinos also pray.
Note the word signals used in comparing statements A and B.

b862083bbc1981bce706.text: We must remember that when comparing, aside from using in like manner and the same with, we can also use other signal words or phrases such as: also, in the same manner, likewise, and similarly.

b04297e5fad741af1fc5.text: How about in statements C and D?  Statements C and D show contrast.  Statement C shows two contrasting ideas: Thais offer cats to ask for something while

f129c98fcc7e109a45a1.text: The first part of the module discussed the purpose of comparing and contrasting. We used the story titled, "My Thai Cat," which is a narrative text, to give a background of the Thai culture. We can use the narrative text as evidence to make your opinion based on what you have read about the Thais’ beliefs and traditions, and compare their culture to our culture as Filipinos. The text that you are going to read next is a Compare-Contrast essay.

5c029a7bc2d24fb05dc6.text: Comparing and Contrasting London and Washington, DC

50c13f72dd30bd4bae8b.text: Both Washington, DC, and London are capital cities of English-speaking countries, and yet they offer vastly different experiences to their residents and visitors. Comparing and contrasting the two cities based on their history, their culture, and their residents show how different and similar the two are.

bfd9851186f87efd78be.text: Both cities are rich in world and national history, though they developed on very different time lines. London, for example, has a history that dates back over two thousand years. It was part of the Roman Empire and known by the similar name, Londinium. It was not only one of the northernmost points of the Roman Empire but also the epicenter of the British Empire where it held significant global influence from the early sixteenth century on through the early twentieth century. Washington, DC, on the other hand, has only formally existed since the late eighteenth century. Though Native Americans inhabited the land several thousand years earlier, and settlers inhabited the land as early as the sixteenth century, the city did not become the capital of the United States until the 1790s. From that point onward to today, however, Washington, DC, has increasingly maintained significant global influence. Even though both cities have different histories, they have both held, and continue to hold, significant social influence in the economic and cultural global spheres.

9f456eb90466a2ccfcb2.text: (The whole essay can be read at https://open.lib.umn.edu/writingforsuccess/chapter/15- 8-compare-and-contrast-essay/)

82cc6e6a2864c0f8a71e.text: The text above is an essay that compares and contrasts the capital cities of the United States of America and the United Kingdom. You can extract information from compare- contrast texts such as this to make opinions or to compare and contrast your own opinion with that of the writer’s. One way to tell if a composition is a compare-contrast text is by looking at the transition signals used, which contribute to the coherence of a paragraph.

ab1b638f942ea369f148.text: What is an opinion? An opinion refers to a view or judgment formed in the mind about a particular topic or issue. Using opinion-marking signals, as discussed in Module 2, you can make your own opinion about a specific topic, issue, or subject matter where one's position or stand is presented. We also compare and contrast our opinion with the texts that we read to self-check if our opinion or argument has a basis. The activities and assessments under the What’s More section of this module will help you develop the skill to make opinions based on a text presented.

7d4761d2a3d0d7f42184.text: To sum it up, for you to effectively compare and contrast your own opinion based on a given familiar text, you have to do the following: 

4380bdbc5e4f8389191f.text: first, identify the similarities and differences between objects, persons, or ideas;  second, take note of the similarities and differences, as well as the transition signals for comparing and contrasting; and  third, express your own opinion by showing comparison and contrast as supported by facts and evidence through the text presented.
